summary: The candidate is correct and complete within its explicitly first-order scope. The active-facet neighborhood argument is valid, the slice-continuity and telescoping transport proofs cover all dimensions including D=1, and fixed-triple pointwise one-sided remainders suffice to pass the support concavity inequalities. Positive facet weights give the stated concavity-gap rigidity. The divergence-theorem equilibrium, injectivity of the translation map, quotient dimension, and the simplex translation and centroid consequences all follow with the claimed quantifiers and without any higher-order conclusion.
